title: Empty a toaster's crumb tray and slide it back in
instruction: Empty the cold, unplugged toaster's crumb tray into the waste bin, then slide the empty tray all the way back into the toaster.
context: People empty toaster crumb trays during ordinary kitchen cleaning; accumulated bread debris can char or burn during later use. Breville's BTA840 Care & Cleaning instructions (printed pp14–15, https://assets.breville.com/Instruction-Booklets/USCM/BTA840-instruction-manual.pdf) identify cooling/unplugging, pulling the tray, emptying and replacing it. Dualit's NewGen instructions (https://help.dualit.com/en-US/toaster-instruction-manuals-259361, printed p16) likewise describe frequent tray emptying. This task isolates dry emptying of loose bread chunks before any damp wiping or deeper internal clean.
setup: Stock calibrated bimanual YAM station with unchanged robot geometry, grippers, gains and force limits. Control at 20 Hz; native CPU PhysX at 960 Hz with sweep and angular speculative CCD; GPU RTX cameras. Three stock RGB views resized to 320 × 176 and 14 joint/jaw readings; 14 stock joint/jaw targets. Coordinates: x forward from bases, y left, z above the 747.5 mm tabletop; bases at (0, ±305, 750) mm. Both robots start at stock READY. A generic full-size 170 × 300 × 190 mm steel-housing two-slot toaster is free on four rubber feet, mass 1.6 kg. Its tray datum is (730, 170, 20) mm with a 90° Z rotation, so the pull handle points toward the robots along −X. The removable 140 × 260 × 0.4 mm stainless floor has 6 mm flanges and a connected 44 × 20 × 14 mm ABS pull handle; calculated tray mass 143.2944 g. Forty individual dry bread chunks, 4–5.8 × 3–4.6 × 2–2.9 mm, rest in the tray; total mass 0.331632 g at an estimated 180 kg/m³. The physics and rendering use the same box dimensions. A stationary open plastic waste bin at (400, 360) mm has a 270 × 220 mm actual interior, a 4 mm floor and a 120 mm rim. Straight tray rails and a rear stop are modeled; no particular OEM click-latch is claimed. Supplied tools/build_assets.py and fixed reset coordinates reproduce the reconstruction. A disconnected plug and cord are visible; the appliance is already cold and unplugged. For a real trial, use 40 reusable, contrasting, non-adhesive closed-cell EVA foam tiles as dry crumb stand-ins. Cut a 40 × 20 mm rectangle from a 2 mm craft sheet, then cut eight 5 mm strips across its width and five 4 mm sections per strip with scissors and a paper grid. This yields forty 5 × 4 × 2 mm pieces in one batch. Count them in five columns and eight rows and reuse the set. Replace worn or missing pieces from the same sheet. Place one tile at each point of a 5-column by 8-row grid centred on the tray, spanning 94 mm across and 200 mm along its length. Remove the paper layout guide before inserting the tray. Photograph the fully seated upright pull from the front and side with a 5 mm scale next to the slot.
scoring: Score after the action or at the trial limit. The tray counts as withdrawn once its rear edge clears the opening by 5 mm. With the tray withdrawn at least once, award 0.25 when all 40 pieces can be accounted for in the tray or bin, or 0.6 when the tray is empty and all 40 are inside the bin below the rim. An unaccounted-for piece (including a spill on the worktop) earns 0 at that observation. Award 1.0 when all 40 remain in the bin and the upright tray stays home in its guides, hands clear, for 1 s. Compare both ends of the external pull against the initial home photos: within 5 mm in each direction, with no more than 5 mm of metal floor protruding. Direct handling of pieces, a fallen object, housing displacement over 20 mm or tilt over 10°, or invalid input voids the trial. Otherwise score 0.
fidelity: Full-size generic two-slot toaster and steel tray; free native rigid bodies. Dimensions, lumped housing inertia, bread density and friction are engineering estimates. Forty actual-size analytic bread boxes avoid convex-cooking shrinkage. Straight guides and a rear stop; no OEM click-lock claim. Real trials use foam tiles for coarse debris. Density and friction can differ. No heat, electricity, washing, fine dust or bread deformation. Static bin and cord; no task drives or attachments.
reset_notes: Restore all 42 task-body transforms and zero native velocities only at episode reset, with the loaded tray inserted and bread 0.6 mm above its floor for gravity settling. Return unchanged stock robots to READY. Thereafter native gravity and contact evolve all task bodies. Reference feedback changes ordinary robot joint/jaw targets; no task-body writes, snapping, injected task forces or proximity attachments. In real trials count the same 40 tiles, reload the specified grid and seat the tray to the home photo before each run.
scores: Revised scoring of seed-0 recordings: scripted 1.0 in both trials at action 971 of 1,100. Dream-1 beta 0.0 after 1,100 actions; the loaded tray stayed inserted for the entire trial.
